instruction:
Work from a terminal with CalculiX 2.21 (`/usr/bin/ccx`). Units: mm, N, MPa, tonne, so a body force needs an acceleration in mm/s^2.

Problem: a flat rectangular plate, 200 mm long (x) and 100 mm high (y), lies in the plane z = 0, is 2 mm thick and is clamped along x = 0. Build ONE deck, `/home/user/Desktop/plate.inp`, that carries three linear static steps, and run it with `/usr/bin/ccx plate` to produce `/home/user/Desktop/plate.dat`.

Model:
- material: linear elastic, E = 210000 MPa, nu = 0.3, density 7.85e-9 t/mm^3; exactly one material
- mesh: 861 nodes at (5*i, 5*j, 0), i = 0..40, j = 0..20; exactly 800 `CPS4` elements, one per 5 x 5 mm cell; node and element numbering are your choice
- one `*SOLID SECTION` covering every element, with the thickness 2.0 on its data line
- node sets with these exact names: `CLAMP` (the 21 nodes at x = 0), `FREE` (the 21 nodes at x = 200), `MIDFREE` (the node at (200, 50)), `CENTRE` (the node at (100, 50))
- boundary conditions: every node of `CLAMP` fixed in dof 1 and dof 2 only (zero); no other boundary condition anywhere, and none added or changed after step 1
- allowed cards: `*Heading`, `*Node`, `*Element`, `*Nset`, `*Elset`, `*Material`, `*Elastic`, `*Density`, `*Solid Section`, `*Boundary`, `*Step`, `*Static`, `*Dload`, `*Node Print` (plus `*Node File`, `*El File`, `*El Print` if you also want .frd output) and `*End Step`; nothing else. No `*NLGEOM`; no `*CLOAD`.

Loads, all through `*DLOAD` (loads persist from step to step unless you remove them):
- Step 1: a uniform tensile traction of 100 MPa in +x on the edge x = 200, applied as element face loads (`P1`..`P4` labels) on the correct faces of the rightmost element column only. In CalculiX a positive face pressure acts INTO the element; work out the face label and the sign from your own element node ordering.
- Step 2: the edge traction removed; instead a uniform body force over the whole plate in -x, applied with the `GRAV` label as `elset, GRAV, g, -1.0, 0.0, 0.0`, with g chosen so that rho*g = 10/200 N/mm^3 (the nominal stress at the clamp is then 10 MPa).
- Step 3: the step-1 traction and the step-2 body force acting together.

Output: in every step, `*NODE PRINT` requests must write to `plate.dat` the displacements (`U`) of set `FREE` and the reaction forces (`RF`) of set `CLAMP`.

CalculiX allows at most 16 entries per data line; split long `*Nset`/`*Elset` lists.

Write `/home/user/Desktop/summary.txt` as exactly one line with four comma-separated numbers, in mm: `ux1, uy1, ux2, ux3`
- `ux1`, `uy1`: mean ux and mean uy over the 21 nodes of `FREE` at the end of step 1
- `ux2`: mean ux over `FREE` at the end of step 2
- `ux3`: mean ux over `FREE` at the end of step 3

The evaluator re-runs your deck independently with `/usr/bin/ccx`, checks the deck and the reported numbers against that run and against the reaction forces in `plate.dat`, and checks that the three steps are consistent with each other. The reported numbers must come from your own run.
